title: The Grievance #1: Form 9
author: anonymous
blurb: Photocopied, folded and stapled off-centre by a human being in a hurry. Thirty-two pages about a man whose only power is that he cannot be made to go away. Sold from a bag, not a shelf, for most of its life. The proprietor of Mint Condition keeps every copy he can find and prices them at almost nothing, and will not discuss why.
source: Scanned from the Mint Condition reading copy, Ironside Street, Coldwater. In-universe fiction.

chapters.title: The Whole Thing
chapters.text:
[The art is photocopied linework, high contrast, some pages copied from copies until the greys have gone to solid black or dropped out entirely. Lettering is hand-printed in capitals with a fine marker. There are no page numbers.]

PANEL ONE. A queue. Seen from behind, receding to a service window under a strip light. Twelve people. The linework thins as it goes back until the people at the front are almost not there.

CAPTION: I AM NOT STRONG. I HAVE CHECKED.

PANEL TWO. A man in the queue. Middle of it. Coat, folder under one arm. Face rendered in about nine lines.

CAPTION: I AM NOT FAST. I AM NOT CLEVER, PARTICULARLY. I CANNOT LIFT A CAR AND I WOULD NOT KNOW WHAT TO DO WITH ONE IF I COULD.

PANEL THREE. The service window. A shutter comes down. WE HEAR IT: a fat black CLACK across the panel.

CAPTION: I HAVE EXACTLY ONE THING.

PANEL FOUR. The queue disperses. Everyone leaves. Everyone.

PANEL FIVE. Same composition. Empty corridor. One man standing in the middle of it with a folder under his arm.

CAPTION: I DO NOT GO AWAY.

—

PANEL ONE. A different day. Same corridor. The queue is back. He is in it.

CLERK: The form's been superseded.

MAN: Then give me the one that superseded it.

CLERK: It's not printed yet.

MAN: Then I'll wait.

PANEL TWO. He steps out of the queue and stands against the wall.

PANEL THREE. Same wall. Later. Same man.

PANEL FOUR. Same wall. Different clerk at the window.

PANEL FIVE. Same wall. The strip light has been changed; you can tell because it is drawn straight now instead of with a kink.

CAPTION: FOURTEEN WEEKS.

PANEL SIX. A hand comes through the window holding a fresh form. The paper is white. It is the only white thing on the page.

CAPTION: FORM 9.

—

PANEL ONE. A room with a table. Two people the other side of it. He is drawn exactly the same size as he was in the queue, which he will be in every panel of this comic, which is the whole joke and the whole point.

OFFICIAL: You understand this doesn't go anywhere.

MAN: It goes to you.

OFFICIAL: And then it goes in a drawer.

MAN: Then it's in a drawer.

PANEL TWO.

OFFICIAL: Do you know how many of these we get?

MAN: No.

OFFICIAL: Nine, last year.

MAN: Nine's not many.

OFFICIAL: Nine is nothing. Nine is a rounding error. Nine is a thing I could lose behind a radiator and nobody would ever ask.

PANEL THREE. Close on the man. Nine lines.

MAN: Then it costs you nothing to take it.

PANEL FOUR. The official takes it.

—

PANEL ONE. Outside. Rain drawn as forty-five degree lines straight across everything, including the figures, because the photocopier could not be trusted with anything subtler.

PANEL TWO. A second man, waiting under the overhang. Younger. No folder.

SECOND MAN: Did they take it?

MAN: Yes.

SECOND MAN: Does that mean anything?

MAN: No.

PANEL THREE. They stand in the rain.

SECOND MAN: Then why?

PANEL FOUR. Full width, thin panel, the two of them small in it.

MAN: Because next year it'll be ten.

—

PANEL ONE. A page of forms, photocopied, overlapping, dozens of them, filled in by dozens of hands. Some in pen. Some in pencil. One in what is clearly eyeliner.

CAPTION: IT WAS TEN.

PANEL TWO. More forms.

CAPTION: THEN IT WAS FORTY.

PANEL THREE. The page is nothing but forms now, layered until the black has closed up.

CAPTION: THEY PRINTED MORE. THEY HAD TO PRINT MORE. THAT IS ALL. THAT IS THE ENTIRE VICTORY AND I AM AWARE OF HOW IT SOUNDS.

—

PANEL ONE. The corridor. Empty.

PANEL TWO. The service window. Shutter down.

PANEL THREE. Taped to the shutter, a printed notice: THIS OFFICE HAS BEEN CLOSED. ENQUIRIES BY POST.

PANEL FOUR. A man standing in front of it with a folder under his arm.

CAPTION: FINE.

PANEL FIVE. He sits down on the floor against the wall and opens the folder on his knees.

CAPTION: I HAVE A PEN.

—

[Back cover, hand-lettered:]

THIS IS NOT A REAL COMIC AND I AM NOT A REAL ARTIST. I AM A CLERK. I HAVE DRAWN THIS BECAUSE NOBODY READ THE FORM AND I THOUGHT SOMEBODY MIGHT READ A COMIC.

COPY IT. I MEAN IT. THE WHOLE THING IS DESIGNED TO SURVIVE A PHOTOCOPIER. IF YOU HAVE ACCESS TO A MACHINE AT WORK AND YOU CAN GET AWAY WITH IT, RUN TWENTY AND LEAVE THEM SOMEWHERE.

DO NOT SELL IT. IF SOMEBODY SOLD YOU THIS, TAKE YOUR MONEY BACK OFF THEM.

WRITE TO: [the address here has been blacked out by hand, in every known copy, with a different pen each time]
